symptom: A brain entry could not record where it came from (which document, which lines), so a requirements UI could neither show the source line behind a requirement nor answer which parts of a document produced none
cause: `Entry` had no provenance field, and the shard's one metadata line is matched by an exact regex (`metaLine`), so extending that line would make every older build report such entries MALFORMED and fail `brain check`
insight: **When a format is shared across versions, place new data where the OLD reader already preserves it.** The Source line goes directly after the metadata line: an older parser takes it as the first body line and keeps it on rewrite (measured: main e4baec63 checks such a store OK and its drop rewrites the line back as `\n\nSource: …`), while lines between title and metadata are silently discarded by old rewrites. The new parser must therefore accept the line after blank lines too — and only as the FIRST non-blank line, or a body that mentions a source becomes provenance. Removing the blank-line skip makes the old-rewrite test read the source as body. Provenance is not content: excluded from ContentKey, stored project-relative, refused outside the project or when missing, and a later-missing file fails check like an anchor naming nothing
